'''Cheryl L. Shavers''' (born December 26, 1953, [[San Marcos, Texas]]) is an American chemist, engineer, and businesswoman. After gaining a degree in chemistry, she worked as an engineer at [[Motorola]]. Shavers returned to university for a few years, gaining a PhD in solid state chemistry, before returning to private industry. Shavers worked at increasingly senior levels in [[Silicon Valley]], at [[Hewlett Packard]] and [[Intel]]. She served as [[Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology|Under Secretary of Commerce for Technology]] in the Clinton Administration (1999–2001), and is a registered patent agent in the [[US Patent and Trademark Office]]. After leaving government service in 2001, she established a consultancy and strategy business, Global Smarts Inc. Shavers was inducted into the Women In Technology International (WITI) Hall of Fame and the Hall of Fame of the Arizona State University's College of Liberal Arts and Sciences.<ref name="TA website Wayback">{{cite web|title=Cheryl L. Shavers, Under Secretary for Technology|url=http://www.ta.doc.gov/shavers.htm|website=Technology Administration|publisher=US Department of Commerce|accessdate=20 February 2017|url-status=bot: unknown|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20000815060257/http://www.ta.doc.gov/shavers.htm|archivedate=15 August 2000}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Shavers' mother, Erna Mae Caldwell, was a maid, who brought her and her sister up alone in South Phoenix in financial hardship.<ref name="Brown 2012">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Jeannette E.|title=African American women chemists|date=2012|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=New York|isbn=978-0199742882|pages=135–142|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wP5Nm-XbEaEC&q=shavers}}</ref><ref name="Fearless" /> She attended [[South Mountain High School]].<ref name="Brown 2012" /> When she was a young teenager, a sex worker in her neighborhood was murdered. Watching the police investigators at the scene gave her the ambition of working in forensic science, which required a chemistry degree.<ref name="Fearless" /><ref name="Brown 2012" />

Shavers was awarded a scholarship to [[Mesa Community College]], and gained a chemistry (Associate Arts) degree.<ref name="Brown 2012" /> She transferred to the [[Bachelor of Science]] program at the [[Arizona State University]], majoring in chemistry and paying for tuition by working at night in a data processing center.<ref name="Fearless" /> Shavers successfully applied for an internship in the Phoenix Police Department's crime lab, working with a team developing a method for separating enzymes trace materials (enzyme typing).<ref name="Brown 2012" /> When the lab director reassigned her to menial tasks a few months short of completing her degree, she resigned in distress and changed career course.<ref name="Brown 2012" /> Shavers graduated in 1976. She has described an encounter as a graduate student with Nobel Laureate, Linus Pauling, at a conference" “He went over some of my work and it all became real".<ref name="Fearless" /> However, she has said she did not want an academic career: "That wasn't for me. I wanted to get going, get back to industry where I could make things happen."<ref name="Reis - Stanford" />

== Career ==

In 1976, Shavers began working in [[Motorola]]'s Semiconductor Sector in Phoenix. Motorola encouraged new graduates to undertake postgraduate studies, and she studied thermodynamics in ASU's chemistry department.<ref name="Reis - Stanford" />

In 1978, she left Motorola for [[Arizona State University]], returning to industry after gaining her PhD in [[solid state chemistry]] in 1981. Her dissertation was titled "Theoretical and experimental studies in crystal chemistry",<ref name="Dissertation">{{cite book|last1=Shavers|first1=Cheryl Lynn|title=Theoretical and experimental studies in crystal chemistry (Dissertation)|date=1981|publisher=Arizona State University|url=http://library.lib.asu.edu/record=b1873080|accessdate=20 February 2017}}</ref> and also published on oxides and nitrides.<ref name="O'Keeffe-1981">{{cite journal|last1=O'Keeffe|first1=M.|last2=Shavers|first2=C.L.|last3=Hyde|first3=B.G.|title=Cation packing and molar volume in oxides and nitrides with the wurtzite structure|journal=Journal of Solid State Chemistry|date=September 1981|volume=39|issue=2|pages=265–267|doi=10.1016/0022-4596(81)90342-X|bibcode=1981JSSCh..39..265O}}</ref>

Her next step was to Hewlett Packard in California, first as a semiconductor process development engineer.<ref name="Reis - Stanford">{{cite book|last1=Reis|first1=Richard|title=Tomorrow's Professor: Preparing for Academic Careers in Science and Engineering|date=1997|publisher=The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|page=Chapter 4|url=https://tomprof.stanford.edu/book/chapter-4|accessdate=20 February 2017|archive-date=26 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170226131159/https://tomprof.stanford.edu/book/chapter-4|url-status=dead}}</ref> At Hewlett Packard, she moved to the Technical Legal Department,<ref name="Brown 2012" /> and became a patent agent in the [[US Patent and Trademark Office]],<ref name="WITI">{{cite web|last1=WITI|title=WITI Hall of Fame Featured profile, Dr. Cheryl L. Shavers|url=http://www.witi.com/center/witimuseum/halloffame/100626/Dr.-Cheryl-L.-Shavers-Chairman-and-CEO-Global-Smarts,-Inc./|publisher=Women in Technology International|accessdate=20 February 2017}}</ref> and spent four years working towards a [[Juris Doctor]] degree at night.<ref name="Brown 2012" /> However, she found the work boring, and decided to go back to science and technology, taking an entry-level managerial position in the diode microelectronics lab at the Wilton company.<ref name="Brown 2012" /> When the company moved, she remained and worked in thin films applications research at Varian Associates.<ref name="Brown 2012" />

Shavers was recruited by [[Intel]] and rose quickly in the corporation to senior management. She also had a weekly "Women in Technology" column for the [[San Jose Mercury News]].<ref name="Brown 2012" /> In 1999, she was nominated by President Bill Clinton to serve as the Under Secretary of Commerce for Technology. In 2001, she left government service and formed a consultancy and strategy company, called Global Smarts.<ref name="Brown 2012" /> Shavers has also produced and hosted radio talk programs,<ref name="Brown 2012" /> and served on the board of directors of several technology companies.<ref name="Press release">{{cite press release|last1=Mentor Graphics Corp|title=Dr. Cheryl L. Shavers Elected to Mentor Graphics Board of Directors|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/dr-cheryl-l-shavers-elected-to-mentor-graphics-board-of-directors-300294414.html|publisher=PR Newswire|accessdate=20 February 2017}}</ref>

== Government office ==

[[File:Senator_Barbara_Mikulski_and_Dr_Cheryl_L_Shavers.jpg|thumb|left|Senator Barbara Mikulski and Cheryl L Shavers, groundbreaking ceremony at NIST in 2000]]
Shavers was confirmed by the US Senate as [[Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology|Under Secretary of Commerce for Technology]] in 1999,<ref name="Shavers appointment">{{cite web|last1=US Senate|title=PN26 — Cheryl Shavers — Department of Commerce|url=https://www.congress.gov/nomination/106th-congress/26?q=%7B%22search%22%3A%5B%22cheryl+l+shavers%22%5D%7D&r=1|website=Congress.gov|date=10 November 1999|publisher=US Congress|accessdate=20 February 2017}}</ref> serving till 2001.

The role of the Under Secretary included overseeing the Commerce Department's Technology Administration (TA) and the Office of Technology Policy (OTP), as well as the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] (NIST), the [[National Technical Information Service]] (NTIS) and the Office of Space Commercialization.<ref name="TA website Wayback" />

As well as providing advice and participating in policy development, she worked on encryption standards and digital signatures to support the development of web commerce during her tenure.<ref name="Fearless">{{cite web |last1=West |first1=Maureen |title=Fearless at the frontier |url=https://magazine.asu.edu/december-2012/articles/alumni-profiles/fearless-frontier |accessdate=20 February 2017 |website=ASU Magazine |publisher=Arizona State University}}</ref>

In her capacity as Under Secretary, Shavers also represented the Department of Commerce in a variety of science and technology forums, including serving as co-chair of the Technology Subcommittee under the U.S.-Egypt Partnership for Economic Growth.<ref name="TA website Wayback" />

== Honors==

* Hall of Fame, Women in Technology International (1996)<ref name="WITI" />
* Hall of Fame, College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (1997)<ref name="Fearless" />

== Personal life ==

Shavers is married to Joseph C Agu.<ref name="Confirmation hearing">{{cite book|title=Nominations of Mr. Johnnie E. Frazier, to be Inspector General; Dr. Cheryl L. Shavers, to be Under Secretary for Technology; and Ms. Kelly H. Carnes, to be Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy, all with the U.S. Department of Commerce; Mr. Albert S. Jacquez, to be Administrator of the Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation; Ms. Ann W. Brown, to be Commissioner and Chairman; and Ms. Mary Sheila Gall, to be a Commissioner, both with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission : hearing before the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, United States Senate, One Hundred Sixth Congress, first session, June 17, 1999.|date=2001|publisher=U.S. G.P.O.|location=Washington|isbn=0160658020|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/009798558|accessdate=20 February 2017}}</ref> She lives in [[Santa Clara, California]], with her husband, daughter, and twin sons.<ref name="Fearless" /> In a 2000 interview with ''Ebony'' magazine, she said, "I have a 4-year-old daughter and I have a responsibility to children between her age and myself to ensure that the trail I'm blazing gets wider and wider".<ref name="Ebony 2000">{{cite news|title=Crossing the digital divide: Black pioneers in the high-tech world|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9doDAAAAMBAJ&q=cheryl+shavers&pg=PA42|accessdate=20 February 2017|work=Ebony magazine|date=June 2000|publisher = Johnson Publishing Company|ref=Page 48}}</ref>
